clips.text_zh: 又見memecoin 吹奏文。PONS話可以翻Pumfun，DOGE1 1% cap就$150M。Normie onboarding浪潮⋯⋯算吧啦，呢啲全部都係我之前輸過嘅pattern 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: PONS & Doge bros. How high can we go? Did the maths: if PONS flips Pumfun, we could see PONS at $3. If DOGE1 captures just 1% of the DOGE market cap, that is already a $150M market cap. Pairing memes with stocks is wild. Boomers who already own stocks can get into crypto with one click.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread hyping PONS token and DOGE1 alongside stocks

signal.rationale: OP is bullish on meme/stock crossover narrative but conviction is speculative

clips.text_en_b2: The PONS and Doge1 crowd are back at it again, spitting out the usual memecoin hopium. I did the maths: if PONS manages to overtake Pumfun, we could see it push past $3, while DOGE1 capturing just 1% of DOGE's market cap already translates into a $150M valuation. Pairing meme tokens with traditional equities is genuinely unhinged, since boomers sitting on legacy portfolios can apparently wade into crypto with a single click.
clips.text_en_c1: Running the numbers on PONS and DOGE1, two memecoins that are generating a remarkable amount of speculative chatter. If PONS somehow manages to flip Pumfun in market cap, a target of roughly three dollars per token becomes mathematically plausible. Meanwhile, capturing even a modest one percent of the Dogecoin market would translate into a hundred and fifty million dollar valuation for DOGE1, a staggering figure for what is essentially a meme asset. The broader thesis is that pairing equities with cryptocurrencies lowers the barrier to entry for normies, particularly boomers whose brokerage accounts already sit a click away from crypto rails.
clips.text_en_c2: Another breathless memecoin manifesto has surfaced, this time courtesy of the PONS and Doge1 evangelists. Run the numbers and the projections border on the hallucinatory: should PONS somehow eclipse Pump.fun's market cap, one could plausibly see PONS at roughly three dollars, while Doge1 capturing a mere one percent of DOGE's circulating value already implies a hundred-and-fifty-million-dollar valuation. The accompanying thesis—that meme tokens can be braided with equity holdings to shepherd normies into crypto via a single click—is, frankly, a rerun of every speculative cycle I have personally been burned by. Still, the underlying psychology remains perversely compelling.

clips.text_zh: SpaceX IPO lockup第三release 9月9號到，319M股解禁，大約2.4% total。噉嘅supply⋯⋯唔怪得最近SpaceX pre-market一直軟。prop firm CFD做空又輸緊 😭 又係學費
clips.text_en_b1: On September 9, 2026, approximately 319 million additional SpaceX shares become eligible for sale. That is about 7% of the baseline pool, or roughly 2.4% of total shares outstanding. This marks the 90th trading day since the IPO and is the third major lockup release event.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on SpaceX lockup expiry dates

signal.rationale: Implied near-term supply overhang on SpaceX post-IPO could drag growth/tech indices

clips.text_en_b2: On September 9, 2026, SpaceX faces its third post-IPO lockup release, with roughly 319 million shares becoming eligible for sale. That figure amounts to about 7% of the baseline pool, or somewhere in the neighbourhood of 2.4% of total shares outstanding, since the 90-day milestone has now been crossed. With that much supply hitting the market, it is hardly surprising the pre-market has been sliding steadily, and my prop firm CFD short is bleeding out yet again.
clips.text_en_c1: The third SpaceX post-IPO lockup release falls on September ninth, at which point approximately three hundred and nineteen million additional shares become eligible for trading. That figure represents roughly seven percent of the baseline restricted pool, or about two point four percent of total shares outstanding, which marks the ninetieth trading day since the listing. The supply overhang this creates helps explain why SpaceX shares on the pre-market have been drifting lower in recent sessions, a soft tape that anyone short via prop firm CFDs is currently learning the hard way. Education is rarely cheap, and tuition in this market is no exception.
clips.text_en_c2: SpaceX's third post-IPO lockup expiration arrives on the ninth of September, releasing approximately 319 million shares into eligibility for sale—constituting roughly seven percent of the baseline pool and a non-trivial 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding. Such a supply overhang, coinciding precisely with the ninetieth trading day since flotation, offers an elegant explanation for the persistent softness observable in pre-market quotations of late. Those of us prop-trading CFD shorts against the name have, predictably, been donating tuition money to the market once again. The pattern, it seems, never ceases to instruct.

clips.text_zh: MIT有Nobel economist出咗篇paper叫Automation and Repression。AI自動化 → 財富集中 → 工人反 → elite鎮壓。ok 所以我做surveying都唔安全？廢柴靠AI續命 🥲
clips.text_en_b1: MIT mathematically proved that AI will destroy democracy. A Nobel-winning MIT economist published a paper called Automation and Repression. As AI and automation replace human labor, wealth concentrates in the hands of a tiny group of capital owners. When inequality hits a critical mass, the ruling elite responds with repression.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread discussing Nobel-winning MIT paper on AI, inequality and repression

signal.rationale: Macro/societal commentary, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: MIT researchers have effectively put a mathematical seal on what many suspected all along: AI is set to erode democratic institutions. A Nobel-winning economist there published a paper titled Automation and Repression, outlining how automation funnels wealth towards a tiny elite while displacing workers. Once inequality crosses a critical threshold, the paper argues, the ruling class inevitably reaches for repressive measures to maintain control.
clips.text_en_c1: An MIT economist with a Nobel on the shelf has published a paper titled Automation and Repression, in which he constructs a mathematical model suggesting that artificial intelligence will, in effect, corrode democratic governance. The mechanism runs as follows: as automation displaces human labor, wealth concentrates in the hands of a narrow capital-owning elite; once inequality crosses a critical threshold, the ruling class resorts to repressive measures to preserve its position. If a Nobel laureate has modelled this trajectory rigorously, then surveying, which I had assumed was relatively future-proof, looks considerably less secure.
clips.text_en_c2: An MIT economist with a Nobel on the shelf has formalised a rather grim syllogism: automation displaces labour, capital accrues to a vanishingly small elite, inequality crosses some critical threshold, and the resulting instability invites repressive governance. The paper, entitled Automation and Repression, marshals mathematical rigour to argue that artificial intelligence does not merely hollow out the middle class—it corrodes democratic legitimacy itself. One is left to wonder, with a certain gallows humour, whether surveying constitutes an endangered profession or merely an undignified one, propped up by algorithms whose indifference is, if nothing else, consistent.

clips.text_zh: Bessent想踩中國補貼，結果全個internet得一句：'BYD is the best $70,000 car that $35,000 can buy'。BYD免費贏到廣告 lol。BYD香港周街都見到，唔關我事，考牌先算 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bessent tried to slam China over subsidies, but the only thing people heard was: BYD is the best $70,000 car that $35,000 can buy. Best free ad for BYD in 2026.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread mocking US official's BYD comment
clips.text_en_b2: Bessent tried to take China to task over subsidies, yet the only line that actually stuck across the internet was a glowing endorsement disguised as criticism: BYD is the best $70,000 car that $35,000 can buy. That single soundbite ended up being the most effective free advertisement BYD could have wished for in 2026, although I doubt anyone in Hong Kong needs convincing, since their cars are plastered across every other street. Whatever, that is their problem.
clips.text_en_c1: When Treasury Secretary Bessent attempted to criticise Chinese industrial subsidies, the narrative he intended to construct was largely drowned out by a single quip that ricocheted across the internet: BYD is the best seventy-thousand-dollar car that thirty-five thousand can buy. The line, which captured the asymmetry between sticker price and perceived value, did more for BYD's brand than any conventional advertising campaign could have hoped to achieve. It was, in effect, the most generous free advertisement the company received throughout 2026, and one that money genuinely could not have bought.
clips.text_en_c2: When Treasury Secretary Bessent sought to chastise Beijing over industrial subsidies, the political theatre collapsed into a single, devastatingly quotable line: that BYD is, ostensibly, the best seventy-thousand-dollar car that thirty-five thousand can procure. The remark, intended as critique, ricocheted across the internet as an unsolicited testimonial, conferring upon BYD what any marketing executive would regard as the apotheosis of earned media—a free advertisement of precisely the calibre money cannot procure. One observes the brand ubiquitously on Hong Kong's streets, though such matters remain, for the moment, peripheral to the more pressing business of obtaining a driver's licence.

clips.text_zh: DON'T NOD執笠，網民話係玩家嘅錯。咁S15都開打緊，戲外game studio都執笠，戲內新patch又ban晒啲meta。Lol 我隻LoL都冇時間打，考牌都未完 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: The Life is Strange developer DON'T NOD is shutting down, and apparently it is your fault because you did not buy their games. Studios keep closing while players keep complaining about patches.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on DON'T NOD studio closure

signal.rationale: Gaming industry news, no trade relevance

clips.text_en_b2: The developer behind Life is Strange, DON'T NOD, is reportedly shutting its doors, and according to the chorus of online commentators, it is squarely the玩家的 fault for not buying enough copies. Studios keep folding one after another while the playerbase carries on moaning about balance patches in season 15. Meanwhile, I cannot even find the time to log into my LoL games, since my driving licence saga is far from finished, so the irony is not lost on me here.
clips.text_en_c1: DON'T NOD, the studio behind the Life is Strange franchise, is reportedly shuttering its doors, with a sizeable contingent of netizens hastening to blame the audience itself for failing to purchase enough copies. The irony is difficult to miss: studios continue to fold while players continue to lament every freshly deployed balance patch. Meanwhile, ranked Season 15 of League of Legends is already underway, meta champions have been nerfed into oblivion, and I have neither the time nor the energy to climb the ladder, particularly given that my driving licence lessons remain unfinished. The game, both in fiction and in reality, appears to be running itself.
clips.text_en_c2: Don't NOD, the studio behind the Life is Strange franchise, is shuttering its doors, and the discourse has predictably devolved into recrimination: the studio's demise is, we are told, the players' own fault for declining to purchase its offerings. The irony is difficult to overstate—studios continue to fold while their audiences lament balance patches and meta reshuffles, as though the two phenomena were unrelated. Season fifteen grinds on, in-game and out. One finds oneself without time even for League, let alone the licence examination that looms with quiet, persistent urgency.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信今日又message我：'315lb bench唔代表乜嘢，grappling先係真嘅'。我話我survey一日已經筋疲力竭⋯⋯btw佢講嘅都有道理，ground game真係會kill你 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Hey nice bench press, 315 lbs really impressive, but a grappler who weighs 50 pounds less than you will fold you in half. You have no reason not to train grappling unless you want some smaller guy to make you his bitch on the ground. Any half-decent grappler would have you staring at your own asshole in seconds.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread pushing grapplers over bench press

signal.rationale: Fitness culture debate, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: My overweight training partner messaged me again today, insisting that a 315lb bench means absolutely nothing because grappling is where the real test lies. He argued that any grappler weighing fifty pounds less would fold me in half, and frankly, he has a point, since mastering the ground game tends to brutalise strength-only athletes. I told him surveying already wipes me out, but the relentless nagging is wearing me down, and I suspect I will eventually cave and drag myself to class.
clips.text_en_c1: My friend, a stocky individual with strong opinions, messaged me again today to insist that a three-hundred-and-fifteen-pound bench press is, in his considered view, largely meaningless, and that grappling才是真正的试金石. His argument, delivered with characteristic confidence, is that any competent grappler who outweighs me by fifty pounds would dismantle me with minimal effort, particularly once the exchange hits the mat. While I remain sceptical, given that surveying already leaves me physically depleted by day's end, I must concede that his reasoning holds water: ground game genuinely does neutralise raw strength, and ignoring it would be foolish.
clips.text_en_c2: The corpulent correspondent has again taken to messaging me with his customary thesis: a 315-pound bench press, however imposing, signifies little when measured against the unforgiving ontology of grappling, where ground game annihilates static strength with metronomic indifference. After a full day's surveying, one can scarcely muster the energy for rebuttal, yet the man is not entirely wrong—technical submission work does, as he insists, humble the uninitiated with humiliating efficiency. There exists an undeniable truth in the proposition that a competent grappler weighing fifty pounds less could, given the opportunity, render one's anatomical geography distressingly novel.

clips.text_zh: 有人推薦我睇CSM漫畫，Reze arc戲院個陣我冇去，但網上個discussion好熱。Panel layout真係好cinematic，season 1方向我覺得OK。 Gundam 00完咗之後終於有新嘢睇 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Chainsaw Man volume 6 and 7. I did not watch the Reze arc movie when it was out in theaters but I always liked season 1, so I recently started reading the manga. I can see why everyone would love the movie so much. The manga is very enjoyable so far, with cinematic panel layouts that match the anime's style.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread recommending Chainsaw Man manga over the movie
clips.text_en_b2: Someone finally pushed me towards the Chainsaw Man manga, and although I missed the Reze arc when it played in cinemas, the online discussion was impossible to ignore. Having enjoyed the first season's direction, I eventually caved and started reading from volume 6 onwards, and it has been an absolute blast so far. The panel layouts feel genuinely cinematic, mirroring the anime's visual flair, so now that Gundam 00 has wrapped, I finally have something fresh to sink my teeth into.
clips.text_en_c1: A friend recently recommended that I read the Chainsaw Man manga, volumes six and seven in particular, which cover the Reze arc that I had conspicuously missed when it screened theatrically. Having enjoyed the first season's animated adaptation, I resolved to catch up via the source material, and the experience has been thoroughly rewarding. The panel layouts are unmistakably cinematic, mirroring the kinetic visual language that made the anime so distinctive, and the story beats translate remarkably well to the printed page. With Gundam 00 finally wrapped up, I find myself, for the first time in months, with a genuinely compelling series to read. Long may it last.
clips.text_en_c2: Having been prevailed upon to sample Chainsaw Man's manga, volumes six and seven in particular, I approached the material with a degree of scepticism, having missed the Reze arc's theatrical run and harboured merely fond recollections of season one's adaptation. The subsequent immersion proved unexpectedly rewarding: Fujimoto's panel compositions possess a genuinely cinematic cadence, choreographing motion and silence with a visual economy that the animated iteration only intermittently approximates. With Gundam 00's broadcast concluded and the palate jaded by repetition, one discovers at last a successor worthy of sustained attention.
